keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «번개는 거대한 전기 불꽃이다(주제)» 와 «번개는 보기에 아름답지만 언제나 조심해야 한다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (lightning is a giant spark of electricity) and the conclusion (lightning is beautiful to watch, but it should always be respected). The green sentences are the answers.

words: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity.
a quick, bright flash made by electricity or fire
amounts of electricity stored in something
electricity jumps between the cloud and the ground
a kind of energy that gives power to lights and machines
This heat makes the air expand very quickly
you will know roughly how many kilometers away the storm is
It can be dangerous, so when you hear thunder, go inside a building or a car.

qs.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
qs.qko: 왜 천둥소리를 듣기 전에 번개를 먼저 보나요?
opts: Because light travels much faster than sound
Because thunder starts long after the lightning ends
Because our eyes are stronger than our ears
evs: Because light travels much faster than sound, we see lightning before we hear thunder.
This heat makes the air expand very quickly, and that creates the sound of thunder.
Here is a useful trick: count the seconds between the flash and the boom.
When the charge becomes strong enough, electricity jumps between the cloud and the ground.
why: 빛이 소리보다 훨씬 빨리 이동하기 때문에 번개를 먼저 보고 천둥소리를 나중에 들어요.
Light travels much faster than sound, so we see the flash first and hear the boom later.

qs.q: In “it should always be respected,” what does “respected” mean here?
qs.qko: «it should always be respected» 에서 «respected» 는 여기서 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: treated with care because it can be dangerous
ignored because it is far away
evs: It can be dangerous, so when you hear thunder, go inside a building or a car.
Because light travels much faster than sound, we see lightning before we hear thunder.
Lightning is a giant spark of electricity.
Lightning flashes about 40 to 50 times every second somewhere on Earth.
why: 바로 앞에서 번개는 위험할 수 있으니 천둥이 들리면 건물이나 차 안으로 들어가라고 했어요. 그러니 여기서 «respected» 는 «위험을 알고 조심스럽게 대한다» 는 뜻이에요.
The sentence before says lightning can be dangerous, so we should go inside. Here, «respected» means treated with care.

qs.q: You count 6 seconds between the flash and the boom. About how far away is the storm?
qs.qko: 번쩍인 뒤 쾅 소리가 날 때까지 6초를 셌어요. 폭풍은 대략 얼마나 떨어져 있나요?
evs: Here is a useful trick: count the seconds between the flash and the boom.
If you divide that number by three, you will know roughly how many kilometers away the storm is.
Because light travels much faster than sound, we see lightning before we hear thunder.
Lightning flashes about 40 to 50 times every second somewhere on Earth.
why: 번쩍임과 쾅 소리 사이의 초(6초)를 세고, 그 수를 3으로 나누면(6 ÷ 3 = 2) 폭풍이 대략 몇 킬로미터 떨어져 있는지 알 수 있어요. 두 문장을 이어야 계산할 수 있어요.
Count the seconds between the flash and the boom (6), then divide by three (6 ÷ 3 = 2). You need both sentences to work it out.

ends: Why does lightning often strike tall buildings?
번개는 왜 높은 건물에 자주 칠까?
How does a rainbow appear after a storm?
폭풍이 지나간 뒤 무지개는 어떻게 생길까?
